The entire cascade had ONE cause, visible in the tail of the log: res://src/modules/items/api.gd did not parse at that instant. Everything else followed from it - 'Could not resolve script res://src/modules/items/api.gd', then 'Cannot infer the type of _ITEMS constant', then 'Could not resolve class ItemsApi', then 'Static function attach_dantian() not found in base QiCultivationApi', repeated down the whole tree. The file's mtime was during my run. So the 357 is a contaminated reading and must NOT be recorded as the program's state - this is precisely the AGENTS.md warning that a full run mid-build reports other agents' in-flight breakage as your own. THE SYSTEMIC FINDING, which is the durable part: one agent writing a file in place makes a 26,545-test run not merely wrong but UNREADABLE, because a parse failure cascades through every dependant and aborts tests that would otherwise report their real result. There is currently no way to tell contention noise from a genuine regression at a glance. RECOMMENDED FIX, in tools/ which I own but am not doing unilaterally mid-flight: a cheap pre-flight parse of every script under res://src before the suite runs, so an unparseable file fails in one second naming the file and the line, instead of after a full run producing 1070 errors nobody can triage. title: The teaching door is circular: the only writer of fit is the verb that refuses you for lacking fit, so no student can ever be taught

Chain: SectApi.teach checks SectTeaching.student_admitted(def, s_ledger), which is def.teaches_at(SectState.fit(student_ledger, def.doctrine_id)), which is student_fit >= def.min_purity. The ONLY production writer of a ledger fit map is SectTeaching.apply_fit (grep for apply_fit across game/src returns exactly one caller, api.gd:484, inside teach). sect_state.gd:313 writes fit too, but that is SectState.normalize -- save-payload normalization on attach, not a verb that grants anything. So the one thing that raises fit is the verb that refuses you for lacking it: a student below the door can never be taught, and therefore can never rise above the door. The suite proves it the only way it can, by hand-writing the ledger: test_sect_teaching.gd:260 and :273 assign (ledger['fit'])[DOCTRINE] directly and re-attach, which is the test doing the player's job -- the same anti-pattern as BL-0101. (a) makes the door reachable with no new content and makes the existing reason string honest; (b) preserves fit as the door but needs an authored grant. Separately worth fixing either way: the reason for a FIT refusal is named standing_below_floor, so a panel would tell a player their standing is too low when their affinity is -- a vocabulary lie in the direction ADR 0083 says is load-bearing for every screen.

title: BLOCKER: WorldAnchor.commit has zero production callers, so no ascent is ever begun and R29-R30 is unreachable

title: A test that could not fail: the discarded-network test never warmed the cache, so a lazy capture grabbed the NEW network and passed
source: body_cultivation agent, found and fixed during the ADR 0057 substitute removal, 2026-10-03
next: A GENUINE TEST DEFECT, found by the agent that removed the last ADR 0057 substitute, and worth keeping because the SHAPE recurs across this program. The test game/tests/modules/body_cultivation/test_body_meridian_read.gd::test_the_provider_never_serves_a_network_the_actor_discarded asserts a provider never serves a meridian network the actor discarded after a save/load. Under mutation M3 - capturing the network on first read instead of resolving it per read - IT STAYED GREEN, 28 passed / 0 failed. Root cause: the test never warmed the stats cache before swapping actor.meridians, so a lazy first read happened AFTER the swap and therefore grabbed the NEW network, which is the correct answer for the wrong reason. A test that only ever reads before the state it is testing has not actually tested the transition. The same shape produced BL-0285 (inventory capacity serialized but never restored, undetected for want of a mutation), BL-0123/0124/0125 (three body gates whose deletion left the suite green) and the tautological test_realm_rate.gd. Whenever the property under test is 'the new value is picked up', the test must establish an OLD value first.

title: The {} summary sentinel is overloaded: a screen bound with nothing supplied is indistinguishable from a screen with no actor
source: orchestrator, by driving all 16 routed screens 2026-10-03
next: THE {} SUMMARY SENTINEL IS OVERLOADED, so a screen that is bound but has nothing supplied reports IDENTICALLY to a screen with no actor at all. Found by driving all 16 routed screens rather than reading them. WHAT I MEASURED: 16 screens are routed in game/src/app/screen_routes.gd. Driving each with --path body --fresh --cmd refresh, 12 returned a populated summary (loot_encounter 38 keys, nation 26, body_cultivation_panel 24, sect 24, mind on its own path 25, qi on its own path 20, tribulation 20, destiny 19, technique_loadout 18, technique_codex 16, item_workbench 15, character 10, crafting 10, world_map 7) and 4 returned {}. I CHECKED MY OWN INSTRUMENT FIRST and was wrong twice. qi_cultivation_screen and mind_cultivation_screen bind perfectly on --path qi and --path mind respectively (20 and 25 keys) - I had driven all sixteen with --path body, so those two were my error. set_bonus_screen and socket_forge are different: BOTH extend UiScreen and therefore INHERIT setup(actor), which is exactly the inheritance trap this session has already cost two false alarms. The composition root binds them with extra shapes my driver does not perform - item_workbench_app.gd:301-306 does screen.call(setup, _actor) AND screen.call(apply_snapshot, SetBonusApi.inspect(_actor)) for ROUTE_SET_BONUS, and :280-282 does screen.call(setup, _actor) AND _forge.bind(screen) for ROUTE_SOCKET, while socket_forge.gd additionally exposes bind_view(view: Dictionary). So all sixteen screens ARE bindable and the driver is the thing that cannot bind four of them. THE REAL FINDING IS UNDERNEATH THAT: the UI standard says summary() returns {} when there is NO ACTOR, and every screen honours that. But a screen that IS bound and has been handed no snapshot also returns {}, because it has nothing to render. Those are different states - not enrolled, versus enrolled with nothing to show - and they render identically, so neither a player nor a headless test can tell them apart. That is the same class as the mind anchor gate reading open when it should read shut, and the same class as a refusal rendering like an offer: a state that is invisible because it is indistinguishable from another. Three questions nobody has decided, which is why this is filed rather than fixed: (1) should the {} sentinel be reserved strictly for no-actor, with a bound-but-empty screen reporting a distinct shape such as bound:true with an empty row list? (2) is apply_snapshot the right seam at all, or should a set-bonus screen read its snapshot through the facade like every other screen reads its state? (3) does the same overload affect any OTHER screen that renders from a pushed-in view rather than from the actor - socket forge and the workbench both qualify, and the workbench summary returned 15 keys so it is probably fine, but nobody has checked systematically. FIX FOR MY OWN INSTRUMENT, which I will do: game/tools/ui_driver.gd needs to perform the same three extra binding shapes the composition root performs, so a screen is driven exactly as the game drives it. A driver that binds a subset of what production binds will keep reporting live features as dead - which is how BL-0320 was filed against the loot screen when the fault was the harness.

title: tools check cannot pass while a run that prints a clean tally still exits 1, because the import pass and the suite have different exit contracts
source: Measured 2026-10-03. tools test returned exit 1 while printing 'Results: 433 passed, 0 failed'. Root cause was NOT a tool defect: a concurrently-written test file (test_event_beat_sink.gd, mtime one second before the check) referenced an undeclared EventDefCatalogProbe, so the engine emitted a Parse Error, _error_lines classified it as an abort, and run_godot returned the engine's code. Every layer behaved correctly. tools/test.py:164 returns result.returncode, and the runner's own quit(1 if total_failed > 0 else 0) is right.
next: No fix needed. The lesson is operational: a green tally beside a non-zero exit means a file changed mid-run, so re-measure rather than trusting the number. Confirm the owning agent has finished writing before reading any scoped suite result.

title: ADR 0109's race gate is enforced on the convenience wrappers, not on the seams every caller passes, and two call paths bypass it entirely
source: lineage program audit 2026-10-03, verified by direct read of the call sites
next: ADR 0109 says 'the three cultivation modules read RaceGate at the breakthrough seam, and nowhere else' and lists only the one-shot attempt_breakthrough / try_breakthrough verbs. Grep and direct read show the gate is on the WRAPPER, and the wrappers are bypassable: game/src/modules/body_cultivation/api.gd:202 begin_breakthrough and :220 resolve_breakthrough call BodyAdvancement.start_attempt / resolve_attempt with NO gate at all, and those two are the documented DURABLE two-phase lifecycle (the pill is spent and the attempt persisted so it can span a save); game/src/app/mind_cultivation_ui.gd:152 calls MindAdvancement.try_breakthrough(_actor) directly, bypassing MindCultivationApi entirely. So a stoneborn (which closes mind_cultivation) can click Breakthrough on that screen and walk into mind cultivation, and can do the same through the durable body path. ADR 0078's finding - 'a race gates nothing' - is only half fixed, and the half that is fixed is the half nobody takes. THE FIX: the gate belongs one layer down, where every caller already passes - BodyAdvancement.start_attempt, MindAdvancement's entry point, and QiBreakthroughTransaction.execute - not in the facade. Then remove the now-redundant facade-level calls rather than leaving two. This is the same shape as the triplication failures ADR 0066 exists to stop: a rule enforced at the convenience surface instead of at the one surface that is unavoidable. Note this is the exact failure the whole lineage programme was built to prevent, recurring one layer up, so it is worth fixing rather than documenting.

title: ADR 0062's anti-convergence claim is decorative: commonborn tops all three axes under the test's own metric, and the cap that permits it was invented in the test file
source: lineage program design audit 2026-10-03, independently recomputed from the .tres files
next: ADR 0062's load-bearing balance claim is that 'race x path is a partition, not a tier list' and that no race is best at everything. Recomputing the shipped content with the shipped metric (game/tests/modules/race/test_race_content.gd:194 _axis_strength) gives commonborn leading ALL THREE axes - QI 1.04, BODY 1.04, MIND 1.04 - because it closes mind (scored -1000), has no realm ceiling, carries a 36500-day lifespan and gives +1.0 to all seven base attributes, while the three specialists give 2-4 on one attribute and nothing elsewhere. commonborn is also the fallback every raceless actor is born into (ADR 0108: 'no actor is ever born raceless'), so the default body is the strongest body. TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS: (1) the threshold is a test-file invention - MAX_TOP_AXES := 2 at test_race_content.gd:19 - and grepping all 111 ADRs for 'top-2'/'two axes'/'more than one axis' finds zero hits, so the test asserts a rule no ADR states; (2) a metric that scores a closed path as -1000 cannot express a body plan, because 'leading an axis you are forbidden to enter' is an artifact of the scoring function rather than a balance property. THE FIX, and it is the one ADR 0062 actually cares about: delete the scoring metric and assert the STRUCTURAL claim instead - every authored race must be refused at least one breakthrough by ADR 0109's gate. That is what the partition means, it is already implemented, and it cannot be gamed by a constant. commonborn will still need a realm ceiling or a narrower affinity set, because as shipped the body everyone is born into is the widest, the longest-lived of the non-stoneborn, and the numerically best on all three axes. This is a content ruling as much as a test fix, so it wants the owner's judgement.

title: An item quest grant is recorded unspent by design, so the quest route stays undeclared and 3076 items remain honestly unobtainable
source: Verified 2026-10-03 at the source, not from the docstring. quest/api.gd:406 calls QuestGrants.pay, which returns {paid, unspent}; quest_grants.gd:20-27 states why item pays nothing: ItemsApi is not a quest dependency and the module does not declare one, so calling it would be an undeclared edge. The grant is recorded as owed and whoever later owns inventory delivery reads it. Fate and destiny DO pay (earn_fate/earn_destiny, ADR 0065). So the module is complete for what it owns; it cannot deliver an item.
next: Whoever owns inventory delivery must read the unspent grants. Until then the audit reporting 3076 quest items as unreachable is CORRECT, and declaring a quest route to make the number green would be the lie. Do not declare the route without a delivery path.

title: tools check short-circuits, so 8 committed E501 stop arch, the ledgers, the data audit, the tests and BOTH incident guards from ever running
source: measured tools lint exit 1 on committed code + tools check stage order from AGENTS.md; audit 2026-10-03 (compounds BL-0370, which is why 	ools fmt cannot clear them either)
next: GATE-ORDERING FRAGILITY, and the most serious finding of the 2026-10-03 audit. tools check runs its stages in order: fmt --check -> lint -> arch -> deferred validate -> backlog validate -> data audit -> test. Because it is a short-circuiting sequence, ANY early stage failing means every later stage never runs. MEASURED: tools lint exits 1 on 8 committed E501 in tools/map_assets.py and tools/map_generate.py (confirmed committed, not in-flight: `git status --short` on both is empty), so `tools check` halts at stage 2 and NEVER REACHES arch, the incident/backlog/deferred ledgers, the data audit, or the tests. That means the two incident guards -- test_no_unbounded_wait.gd (INC-0001 disk) and test_no_deferred_free.gd (INC-0002 memory) -- are not executed at all by the gate that is supposed to run them, purely because one agent left 8 long Python strings unformatted. COMPOUNDS BL-0370: those same 8 lines are exactly the class `ruff format` provably cannot fix, so running `tools fmt` does not clear them either. The hazard is therefore not one agent's untidy Python; it is that the safety guards sit DOWNSTREAM of a stage that unrelated routine work can red-flag, so a cosmetic failure silently disables every guard after it. SECOND, SAME SHAPE: arch_rules is itself RED on arrival, 2 pre-existing failures in test_arch_rules.gd because it asserts `tools arch` still warns about `src/app/consumable_system.gd` and that file no longer exists (game/src/app now holds 15 .gd files). The warning went quiet, which is exactly the 'a guard that stopped firing reads like a clean tree' failure mode that test's own comment warns about. NET: the gate cannot currently be used as a green/red signal at all, because two of its stages are red for reasons unrelated to what they gate. NEXT: decide whether the safety guards must run BEFORE the cosmetic stages rather than after them, since a guard that can be switched off by an unrelated lint error is not a guard. That is a change to the order in tools/check.py, so it needs an ADR.

title: One agent mid-writing tools/data.py takes down every tools subcommand for every agent
source:
Measured 2026-10-03 during the acquisition-route and event-validator work. tools/data.py
was observed at 2314 lines mid-write and the loader reported an unterminated string
literal at line 889 while the file at that instant held different text on that line,
which is the signature of a torn read rather than a real syntax error.
next:
Every "uv run python -m tools" subcommand died while one agent was mid-write on
tools/data.py, because data.py is imported by the loader each subcommand uses. One
agent's single edit took fmt, lint, arch, data audit and test down at once for every
concurrent agent. The reported line number pointed at a region that did not match the
file's real content at the same instant - the loader read a torn snapshot - and a
direct ast.parse of the same path succeeded minutes later with no edit in between.
Treat "every tools command is unavailable" as transient and re-verify the file parses
before reporting it as a defect. A structural fix would move the route table into its
own module so the loader's import graph is smaller, but that is a refactor with its
own risk and is not owed while agents are in flight.

title: A single mid-write file in tools/ takes the whole toolchain down, so a gate reading red during concurrent edits is not evidence of a defect
source: Measured 2026-10-03. tools/data.py was 45 lines mid-edit and tools/__main__ refused to load: 'unterminated string literal (line 889) ... every tools command is unavailable until it loads.' That killed fmt --check, lint, arch, data audit and every tracker write at once, while the SAME file parsed cleanly under a direct ast.parse microseconds later (the loader had read a stale snapshot). Two distinct false reds in one hour, both from reading a moving target: (1) tools test printing '433 passed, 0 failed' and exiting 1, which was a file written one second earlier plus, in a second instance, godot.lock contention from my own overlapping runs; (2) fmt reporting 6 files to reformat that agents were actively writing.
next: When a gate stage reads red while agents are in flight, check the file's mtime and parse it directly before believing the message. Never fix a moving file: reformatting or repairing it edits another agent's work mid-write. Wait for mtime to stabilise, then re-measure.

title: Deferring to a live agent is only sound when re-measured: a finished owner left the map gate blocked for hours
source:
Measured twice in one session, opposite outcomes. tools/map_assets.py had been
reported as "owned by a live external agent" for hours; checking git status showed
the file COMMITTED and CLEAN with no write for 90 minutes, and its last commit was
db4fc412. The agent had finished and left, so the deferral was protecting nothing.
Conversely game/src/modules/combat_engine/body_wounds.gd was genuinely dirty and
written 45 seconds before the same check. The two states look identical from the
conversation and only the filesystem distinguishes them.
next:
Never report a file as owned by a live agent from memory or from an earlier
measurement: re-check `git status --short -- <path>` and its mtime before deferring,
and say so with the timestamp. A deferral with no timestamp is indistinguishable from
a real blocker and silently stalls the gate. After fixing a file yourself, verify
which of the OTHER findings are genuinely live the same way rather than assuming the
first sample generalises.

title: The body ascent defect was the missing progress ROW, not missing wording: the unmet list always stated the gate
source:
The orchestrator reported the defect as "the player is owed an ascent and the screen
says nothing about it" and "renders no ascent wording". BOTH were overstated, and the
second body-ascent agent repeated them. Measured against the before-state: unmet[]
already carried "Walk the ascent: 4 of 4 steps to walk", so the player WAS told a gate
existed. What was missing was the ascent ROW - the progress bar and the "4/4" position.
The player was told a gate existed with no indication of how far along the walk they
were. Separately, the claim that the finished-walk branch was also dead is false:
outstanding == "" requires a completed AscensionState, which makes ascension_ok true,
which makes required false, so that branch never matched the first required test - its
assertion was PASSING AT BASELINE. Only the owed case was dead.
next:
Describe a rendering defect by what the node actually contained, not by what the screen
"failed to say". Read the before-drive output verbatim: unmet[] is rendered text too.
When reporting a dead branch, check whether the predicate can reach it before calling it
unreachable - a branch whose assertion passes at baseline was never the defect.

title: The body ascent defect was a missing ROW, not a missing requirement: the sentence was already on screen inside unmet
source:
I briefed both body-ascent agents that "the player is owed an ascent and the screen says
nothing about it". That was false. The before-drive already carried "Walk the ascent: 4 of
4 steps to walk" inside the `unmet` list: the requirement sentence WAS on screen. What was
missing was the ascent ROW - the bar and the player's position in the walk. A player was told
a gate existed, with no progress toward it and nothing stating how far they had come. The
correct defect statement is "no row", not "no wording", and the fix is keyed on `outstanding`
alone so the row can exist.
next:
When briefing a defect from a summary, verify the rendered node AND the read model before
stating what is missing; a populated field and a blank node are different defects with
different fixes. This agent measured it and corrected two of my claims: the `""` branch was
reachable (a completed AscensionState makes required false, so the test never matched) and its
assertion passed at baseline - only the owed case was dead.

title: At the terminal realm an unwalked ascent states a requirement beside a button that is never offered
source:
At the terminal realm an ascent that has not been walked yields required == false while
outstanding is still non-empty, so the screen states a live requirement beside a control
that is not offered. Reached through normal play only if reaching R30 stops requiring
is_complete(); currently unreachable because R30 requires it, and reachable only through
a doctored save. The two halves disagree in body_cultivation/api.gd's required and in
core's ascension_ok terminal exemption, so neither could be fixed from the ui/ files that
owned the row. This is the same "requirement with no affordance" shape that 39b148ef
raised for the NO_ASCENT case.
next:
Decide which of the two owns the terminal exemption: if the walk is genuinely owed at the
terminal realm, ascension_ok must keep required true; if it is genuinely waived, the row
must stop stating it. The split is deliberate in neither place, so one of them is wrong.
Reachable-by-doctored-save does not mean unreachable, and a save editor is not the threat
model here - a player who completes the ladder by an unintended route is.

title: The acquisition count fell 4132 to 1553 because HEAD counted every craft-only item as a delivered root, not because craft stopped working
source: tools data audit on one unchanged tree: 7981/7982 obtainable in the content graph, 1553/7982 deliverable by shipping code, exit 0. HEAD (9b26fc45) reports 4132 for the same tree. Cause, measured by loading HEAD and the working tree side by side: HEAD _runtime_roots does 'if kind == craft: continue', which leaves source_type None, so an item whose ONLY source is craft: lands in roots outright and its recipe never has to close. 2791 craft-only items were counted that way and only 216 are reachable through the recipe closure; the other ~2575 rest on inputs no shipping route delivers. HEAD also contradicted its own _obtainable, which deliberately excludes craft from root_types. Roots 4087 vs 1296, reachable 4132 vs 1553. tools/data.py is being edited concurrently (sha changed twice inside one 60s poll), so this fix is uncommitted in-flight work by another agent.
next: When a measurement moves, diff the two implementations rather than reasoning about the delta: importing HEAD and the working tree in one process and comparing roots/reachable named the craft branch in a single run. Never commit a file another agent is actively writing - hash it twice 10s apart first.

title: CORRECTION: the 4132-of-7982 deliverable figure was wrong; the honest number is 1553
next: DO NOT READ 1553 AS A REGRESSION FROM 4132. The old figure was a measurement bug, not a loss of routes. _runtime_roots did 'if kind == craft: continue', leaving source_type None, so 2791 craft-only items were counted as roots outright WITHOUT their recipe ever closing - which contradicted _obtainable in the same file, since _obtainable deliberately excludes craft from root_types. Only 216 of those 2791 are actually closable; spot-check A10_immortal_axletree_aged has inputs _refined, X23_immortal_moidores_tannin and Q7_immortal_dill_warp, all unreachable. The remaining 6429 split gather 821, quest 1392, gather+quest 4150, unreachable input 66. title: A parse error in another agent's in-flight nation/api.gd stops the whole app loading, so every suite that mounts ItemWorkbenchApp reports a false green
source: uv run python -m tools test --suite test_item_pipeline on an otherwise unchanged tree: 58 passed, 0 failed while 23 of 81 tests never ran, because SCRIPT ERROR: Parse Error: Cannot find member R_NOT_A_POLITY in base NationState (referenced at game/src/modules/nation/api.gd:583; nation_state.gd declares R_NOT_A_PARTY and no R_NOT_A_POLITY) cascades into Failed to load script res://src/app/item_workbench_app.gd. Two more parse errors in the same file: Static function act() not found in base NationApi, and a Variant-inferred local treated as an error. Unmodified since 18:47 and still red at 19:35. The shape is the dangerous one: _boot() returns early on boot_error, so the suite prints 0 failed and the drop-claim assertions never execute - a green that skipped the claim is what AGENTS.md calls a dead seam.
next: The nation owner lands their own file; nothing in tests/ or ui/ is at fault. Until then no result from a suite that mounts the app can be trusted, so compare the passed count against the suite total before believing a green. Do not fix another agent's file to turn the gate green: R_NOT_A_POLITY may be an intended NEW refusal reason distinct from R_NOT_A_PARTY, so a mechanical rename would silently change their semantics.
